notes: LABEL statement (plain and SPLIT=), PROC MEANS with CLASS/OUTPUT, and a user-defined PROC FORMAT (character and numeric ranges) applied via PROC PRINT FORMAT=. Original read score_data.xlsx via PROC IMPORT and wrote a permanent format catalog to a hardcoded local path; replaced the import with an inline sample and kept the format definition WORK-library scoped (dropped the permanent libname section, which pointed at the author's local disk). One small fix applied to the SPLIT= label block: the source wrote `Label Score1 = "Math" * "Score"` (two literals joined by a bare *), which is invalid SAS 9.4 -- the LABEL statement's right-hand side must be a single quoted string, and SPLIT="*" expects the split character embedded inside that one string. Confirmed via sas-expert (verdict: FIX, not a Jenner bug; SAS 9.4 LABEL/PROC PRINT SPLIT= docs) before adjusting to the idiomatic `"Math*Score"` form; the rest of the script is unmodified.
